head: 1e0e1254a4b09faa5b1e0532ccfbf09f0a45dd5e
non_blocking: S-N1: validate.py:7-9, the anchor_self_tests docstring, the commit message and the PR body say a class that ECMA-262 and Python end in different places is refused, but only a $ inside the disputed stretch is refused ([]$]). ^[]a]$, ^[]]$, ^[^]a]$ and ^[^]]$ still compile and run with Python's reading, unchanged from base (R05, R16). Narrow the wording or refuse []/[^] outright.

S-N2: check_all never compiles patternProperties keys (jsonschema_subset.py:126-133), so the _ecma_anchors docstring's 'check_all refuses it' holds for pattern only. A []$] key passes the gate when unexercised and crashes validation with an uncaught re.error when exercised (R10). Pre-existing gap. Compile keys through _pattern in _check and add a self-test.

S-N3 (latent, fail-closed): the sweep requires every anchored pattern that accepts 'verse' or 'id' to reject it plus a newline, which ECMA-262 does not require when the body can match a newline. An added ^[^/]+$ fails the gate twice, although V8 accepts 'verse\n' for it (R11). No shipped (58) or integration-tip (60) regex triggers it. Skip patterns whose body fully matches the planted value.
S-N4 (latent): the sweep filter not p.endswith('\\$') (validate.py:188-189) also drops a pattern such as ^a\\$ whose final $ is a real anchor. No shipped pattern ends that way (R05 B).

S-N5: validate.py:7-8 reads as if every anchored pattern were exercised. The sweep reaches 19 of 58 shipped regexes plus 2 targeted ($defs/id, ^[A-Z]$), though the fix itself holds for all 58 (R05 B: 28,687 accepted-value-plus-newline pairs rejected at head, all accepted at base). Say 'that accepts the planted value'.

S-N6: jsonschema_subset.py:8 says 'with no flags', but JSON Schema 2020-12 core 6.4 recommends the u flag. The anchor rule is unaffected: head matches V8 under both no flag and u on 512,024 pairs (R05 C). Say 'without the m flag'.

S-N7 follow-up (confirmed, pre-existing, outside #132): Python and ECMA-262 \s differ. Python adds U+001C-U+001F and U+0085 and lacks U+FEFF, so the shipped uri pattern ^https://[^\s]+$ accepts a trailing U+FEFF and rejects U+001C and U+0085, both against ECMA-262 (R05 D). Also neither bridged nor refused: []/[^] classes, an authored \Z, and Python-only syntax ((?#...) comments, inline flags; (?#[)^a$ even hides its $ from the class scan). None is in a shipped schema. Suggest one contract-fix so check_all refuses or bridges them.

S-N8 (judgement calls): Duplicated Code in the bare-SchemaSet probe set-up (validate.py:172-174 and 200-201); _ecma_anchors returns a rewritten pattern but reads like a lookup; checker_self_tests is 55 lines because its case table grew (disclosed in the PR).

Merge note: integration has moved to 910910a594f131a8082c355412aefed2b9348e41 (S01 #127, T02c #131), and the PR is BEHIND. An uncommitted merge preview passes the contract gate with counts equal to integration alone apart from the self-tests (53 to 101), with no newline-ending contract value and both new T02c regexes plain ^...$ (R13, R14). Update the branch, confirm patch-id 332880565f3263269b30caeceaf4d0f1c01ee79b and green three-OS checks on the new head, then close #132 by hand.
